To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

single-step reaction norm models can be used for genomic evaluations of yearling weight (the trait studied) in Nelloree cattle, that genotype by environment interaction was observed for this trait, and that the inclusion of genomic data in the model improved the ability to accurately estimate genetic merit for this trait.

single-step genomic reaction norm models were able to detect the existence of G×E for yearling weight and predict genetic values in different production environments, and that genomic regions associated with yearling weight and the environmental gradient were identified.

the use of genomic information in the reaction norm model improved the ability to rank animals according to genetic merit and the reaction norm model was able to identify genomic regions that are associated with different production environments.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of G × E in yearling weight using reaction norm models and genomic information.
the use of reaction norm models to identify G × E for YW in beef cattle.
the identification of genomic regions associated with genotype by environment interaction for YW.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the reaction norm model with genomic information is the most efficient method to identify animals that perform well in different production environments.
the use of genomic information in the reaction norm model improved the accuracy of the prediction of genetic merit for the yearling weight of Nellore cattle.
single-step GBLUP reaction norm model was able to detect G × E for YW in Nellore beef cattle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
single-step GBLUP is a promising method to estimate G×E for YW in Nellore beef cattle.

the use of genomic information in the reaction norm model improves the accuracy of the estimated genetic values, and that the reaction norm model seems to be a good approach to identify genomic regions related to the environment gradient.

the inclusion of genomic data improved the prediction of animals' genetic values for YR, and the use of reaction norm models was capable of identifying the existence of genotype by environment interaction for YR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inclusion of genomic relationship information in reaction norm model improved the prediction ability for future animal performance.
the reaction norm model can be used in beef cattle breeding programs to predict genetic values in different production environments.
genomic information improves the prediction of animals' future performance in reaction norm models.
